newsitem.title: USA: Florida police in 'sexual predator' case punished.
newsitem.headline: Florida police in 'sexual predator' case punished.

text.p: One Florida police officer was fired and another was suspended and demoted on Friday for their handling of a case involving an accused "sexual predator" alleged to have later killed two girls.

Broward County Sheriff Ron Cochran said Detective Deborah Cox was terminated and Sergeant William Robshaw was given a 30-day suspension without pay, removed from a list of candidates for promotion and demoted to deputy. He said the two had failed to arrest Howard Ault, a man labeled a "sexual predator" by the legal system, in a timely manner.

Ault was arrested in November and charged with the kidnapping and murder of two Florida sisters, Alicia Sybilla Jones, 7, and DeAnn Emerald Mu-min, 11, of Oakland Park, Fla., whose bodies were found in the attic of his home. He also was charged with sexually assaulting the older girl.

Another 11-year-old girl had accused Ault of assaulting her on Dec. 31, 1995, in a case assigned to Cox and Robshaw. But they did not arrest Ault on that charge until after the two girls were killed, although he was under house arrest for still another attack on a young girl when he was arrested.

Cochran said an internal review determined that Cox and Robshaw had not acted properly by failing to take Ault into custody more quickly. "No efforts were made to apprehend Ault although probable cause existed for his arrest and his whereabouts could be easily ascertained," he said.

"Although no one has a crystal ball to know what may have happened differently regarding the deaths of the two little girls, Detective Cox and Sergeant Robshaw failed to properly handle what was a relatively uncomplicated case for two seasoned investigators," Cochran said.
A Sheriff's Office spokesman said the two officers had the right to appeal to an arbitration panel.
